## What was built

A layered CSV parser in MoonBit under the root `csv` package, with the required `@csv.parse` / `@csv.print` entry points kept thin and the parsing split into single-responsibility packages:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [csv.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/csv.mbt) | Public facade — `parse` and `print` only |
| [lexer/scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/lexer/scanner.mbt) | Field scanner: unquoted fields, quoted fields, `""` escapes, record boundaries |
| [parser/parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/parser/parser.mbt) | Record assembly + rectangular-record validation |
| [format/writer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/format/writer.mbt) | Minimal-quoting writer (inverse of `parse`) |
| [types/error.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/types/error.mbt), [types/token.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/types/token.mbt) | `ParseError` and the `ScannedField` / `FieldTerminator` vocabulary |
| [README.md](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/README.md) | Architecture, algorithm, dialect, tests, design decisions |

**Parsing model:** the scanner works on `StringView` UTF-16 **code units** (all CSV structure is ASCII, so slicing can never split a surrogate pair and field values stay zero-copy views), and returns one decoded field plus *why it stopped* (`Separator` / `Boundary` / `EndOfInput`). The record driver is then pure cursor movement: CRLF counts as one boundary, a trailing boundary adds no record, a trailing comma adds an empty field, a blank line is a one-empty-field record, and empty input is zero records. LF/CRLF/CR are all accepted.[^1] Quoting is validated, not guessed — unterminated quotes, `"` in an unquoted field, text after a closing quote, and `\"` escapes are rejected, and records must match the first record's width.[^2]

## Implementation (root `ini` package, one responsibility per file)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| [ini.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini.mbt) | `pub fn parse` entry point |
| [ini_scan.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini_scan.mbt) | char predicates, LF/CRLF line splitting, separator/comment/backslash scanning, quote unwrapping |
| [ini_section.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini_section.mbt) | header parsing + key validation |
| [ini_value.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini_value.mbt) | escape table per carrier, quoted values, unquoted values with continuations |
| [ini_parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini_parser.mbt) | entry parsing + document assembly (single pass, global/section state) |
| [ini_printer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini_printer.mbt) | `pub fn print` (values always double quoted) |
| [ini_error.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_2/ini_error.mbt) | `IniError(String)` with `line N: …` messages, plus `IniError::message` |

Key dialect rules are real parser logic, not fixtures: first `=`/`:` wins; `;`/`#` are comments when full-line or after whitespace; quoted values close on the same physical line (an escaped quote cannot close) and reject trailing text; each carrier decodes only its own escapes (`\P` stays `\P`); continuation is decided by the **parity of the trailing backslash run before escaping**, joins the next line directly while keeping whitespace before the marker, and a continuation line contributes text, not syntax; headers end at the first `]` with quotes as ordinary characters except one fully wrapping pair; keys are verbatim, non-blank, control-char free. Malformed input raises with the offending line number.

Key design points (all general, nothing fixture-specific):
- **Outside-in splitting** — each delimiter is resolved at its own layer (`#`, then `?`, then a *grammar-checked* scheme, then a leading `//` authority), so `g:h` is absolute while `./g:h` is relative.
- **Allow-list validation per production** with a real `% HEXDIG HEXDIG` scanner; non-ASCII must arrive percent-encoded.
- `path-noscheme` is enforced (no `:` in the first segment without a scheme), which is how invalid schemes such as `1http://…` and `ht_tp://…` are rejected rather than read as paths.
- **Ambiguous authorities raise** (two `@`, two `:` outside a literal, junk after `[::1]`); empty `host`/`port`/`userinfo` stay `Some("")` (the property generator produces them).
- **IPv6 is validated by counting 16-bit pieces** (`h16` = 1, IPv4 tail = 2, only last), so `::` elision, `[::]`, `[1:2:3:4:5:6:7::]` and `[::ffff:1.2.3.4]` are right while `[:::], [1::2::3], [::1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8], [12345::1]` are rejected.
- **Dot-segment removal** implements the RFC's two-buffer walk, with the output buffer kept as a list of moved pieces so case 2C ("remove the last segment and its preceding `/`") is a `pop`; the base path is used as-is when the reference path is empty, exactly as §5.2.2 states.

## Judgment calls (documented in the README)

- Schemes are lowercased (the RFC allows it and the spec permits it); nothing else is normalized and nothing is decoded.
- Validation is strict ASCII: raw non-ASCII, `"<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, controls, and brackets outside an IP-literal are rejected.

- Multiple `@` in an authority and text after an IP-literal's `]` are errors, not guesses.
- Zone IDs accept both `%25en0` and the widely emitted `%eth0`; port range is not checked (scheme-specific).

Key design points: closure of inline tables and static arrays is enforced by *representation* (finished `Leaf` values); each scanner stops at the first foreign code unit so the statement layer rejects `1.2.3`, `falsify`, `2020-01-01x`; a 256-level nesting guard turns pathological depth into a parse error instead of a stack overflow.

### Algorithm
* **Lexer** – three states (`FieldStart`, `RecordEnd`, `Finished`) plus `pos`/`length`/`field_expected`. One token per *field*: unquoted fields are sliced in one copy, quoted fields splice literal runs around `""` escapes, and the closing quote must be followed by `,`, a terminator, or EOF (that check is what rejects `"a"x`, `"a" "b"` and backslash escapes). * **Parser** – single pass, one record buffer, first-record width as `expected`; equal widths are enforced per `specs/csv.md`, `Eof` with nothing pending adds no record (`""` → zero records, `a,` → two fields, `"\n"` → one empty field).
* **Writer** – quotes only `,` `"` CR LF, doubles inner quotes, LF after every record (so `[[""]]` ↔ `"\n"` round trips).

## Behaviour notes

- Strict per-production validation rather than a blacklist, so unseen invalid inputs are rejected: spaces, `<>"`, `\`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{}`, `|`, control/DEL, raw non-ASCII, bad percent triplets, non-numeric ports, malformed IPv6/IPvFuture/zone literals, invalid schemes, ambiguous authorities (`a@b@c`, `host:80:80`, `[::1]x`).
- No normalization at parse time (dot segments, percent-encoding case and scheme/host case are preserved), which keeps `parse(to_string(u)) == u` exact; scheme case is deliberately preserved, which the public test explicitly allows.
- `Uri::resolve` is literal §5.2: `http:g` stays `http:g`, and the pseudocode's quirks are honoured and tested (`g:c/../d` → `g:/d`; `g//../h` → `.../g/h`).
